vm_tools: Make X sommelier scale internal displays differently X11 applications historically use DPI to decide their scaling, however this does not work for laptops, which are closer to you and so usually have a higher DPI. To solve this problem, the X server usually lies about the DPI of laptops. We emulate this behaviour for chromeos by applying a scale factor if the display is the internal one. We choose 0.66 semi-arbitrarily (based on measuring sample laptop/desktop screen distances in our office). Whilst this fixes some devices, it breaks others, base on a pre-existing bug in sommelier where it would choose a DPI bucket that is no higher than the true DPI. E.g. the pixelbook2's DPI of 232 would be rounded to 160 (not 240) which looks correct, because we werent applying the laptop-distance scale, whereas another device's 168 DPI would be rounded to 160, which looks unusually big (96 would be better), because we werent applying the laptop-distance factor which means the "ideal" DPI for that device is actually 112, closer to 96. BUG=chromium:965817, chromium:973256, chromium:969462 TEST=/usr/share/code/code; \ /opt/android-studio/bin/studio.sh Change-Id: I55d2b09cf72bfbcde8dce135dd239de843cd802a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1716347 Tested-by: Nic Hollingum <hollingum@google.com> Commit-Ready: Nic Hollingum <hollingum@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org>

dlcservice: Contact to update engine for status with newer DBus API Update engine DBus API exposes a newer |GetStatusAdvanced()| which uses |update_engine::StatusResult| proto type. This change is for dlcservice to contact update engine only through this newer DBus API from the previous |GetStatus()| which took all the arguments which are wrapped within |update_engine::StatusResult|. Even with new fields added to |update_engine::StatusResult|, dlcservice will require no change unless a need for using the new addition fields are required. shill: routing_table_entry: Remove from_rtnl field Previously, the from_rtnl field was set when a route was learned about by listening to rtnl messages (rather than coming from a client within shill). This distinction provides little value, and the code currently performs no useful logic with regards to whether or not the field is set. The primary user of from_rtnl is test code, which explicitly sets from_rtnl to fake that a RoutingTableEntry came from RoutingTable::ParseRoutingTableMessage. If in the future we would like to distinguish between routes from different clients or for different purposes, the protocol field would be a more useful, appropriate, and kernel/rtnl-supported means of doing so. BUG=None TEST=All unit tests are passing. Change-Id: Ic21f3643f62d5f0613f939ca4b828782aa40274a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1731350 Tested-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org>
